set.st: July 1939: the three young Belote boys dug up a drain tile holding $1,880 in $5/$10/$20 gold (1882-1902) on the farm 4-4½ mi NW-W of Bronson, on the Matteson-Bronson township line; days later Frank Belote kicked up an iron pipe with $1,120 in gold 12 ft away. A second tile, plugged with concrete at both ends, which the boys had used as a toy smokestack, was never found again. Owner Kregger ordered no more digging and evicted the Belotes. The original owner, who died 17 Apr 1909, was said to have buried several lots of gold; a buried safe was dug up on the farm soon after his death, between Apr 1909 and Mar 1910, and the owner had plowed up a pipe of gold the year before the tile find. Pin is on the farmsteads at the township line, not the spot itself. In Jan 1941 Judge Renshaw split the about $2,900-3,000 found in 1939 half to the finders and half to the heirs of the former owners. The AP account puts the $1,100 in a tin can under the front porch and adds a third cache of $100. The local papers add: it was the old Canaris 'Canary' Phillips farm (Canarius Napoleon Phillips, 22 Aug 1829 - 17 Apr 1909, buried in Matteson; his widow Alzina died 4 Feb 1921, the source of the papers' '1921'), bought by Kregger from a Chicago man. The tile lay barely under the surface in an open field near a clothes-line standard; a pipe plowed up the year before had been tossed in a fence corner; a small safe of money was unearthed soon after Phillips's death, c.1909-10. The Free Press said Phillips 'banked most of his solid cash in secret places of burial about his farm'. The gold was legally the Phillips estate's, hence the 1941 split. A 1941 Free Press recap totals $1,800 + $1,000 + $100 = $2,900 (the Enquirer said $3,000). No later find was reported through 1965.

src: Coldwater Daily Reporter, 11 Oct 1909, p. 2 (Newspapers.com 1370394107): administrators appointed, estate of Canaris N. Phillips; 18 Mar 1910, p. 2 (1370229225): final settlement
